done_when: forge sync installs Forge's git hooks in the folder git actually uses (core.hooksPath when set) and still runs the hooks already there, forge doctor reports a hooks folder without them, and a test proves both with a Husky-style hooks path

findings.body: The fixture uses plain echo scripts, so it misses the hook-preservation failure in the motivating Husky setup. In the inspected src/forge/sync.py, lines 324–327 rename existing hooks to `<name>.pre-forge`, and line 70 executes that renamed file. [Husky's dispatcher](https://github.com/typicode/husky/blob/main/husky) derives the user-script name from `basename "$0"`. Consequently, the renamed wrapper looks for `.husky/pre-commit.pre-forge` instead of `.husky/pre-commit` and silently exits successfully when it is absent; pre-push behaves likewise. Forge's guards run, but the existing Husky checks are skipped. Preserve Husky's dispatch behavior and extend this CLI test to exercise its wrapper and assert that the actual user hooks execute. The current echo fixture passes despite this unmet Done-when requirement.
findings.title: Not done: prove forge sync preserves existing Husky hooks

why: In a repo whose git hooks folder is set elsewhere, such as Husky's .husky/_ in myclaw, forge sync installs its git hooks where git never runs them, so Forge's commit and push guards are off
